title: Move Less, Retrieve Fast: A Retrieval-in-Memory Architecture for Language Models
problem: Retrieval-augmented language models (RALMs) suffer from substantial data movement and irregular access patterns during retrieval, limiting efficiency on conventional CPU/GPU architectures.
motivation: RALMs are increasingly deployed for knowledge-grounded inference, but retrieval bottlenecks (data movement and irregular memory access) prevent practical deployment at scale.
method: Rimast architecture combines 3D-stacked processing-in-memory (PIM) hardware with hardware-software co-design. Hierarchical PIM dataflow minimizes data transfer between memory and compute. Software layers include skew-free data mapping for uniform distribution and adaptive offloading strategies to handle irregular access patterns in RALM retrieval.
key_novelty: First PIM architecture specifically optimized for RALM retrieval via hierarchical dataflow and skew-free mapping, achieving 273× speedup over CPUs.
contributions: Hierarchical PIM architecture with retrieval-in-memory dataflow minimizing data transfer
Skew-free data mapping addressing irregular retrieval access patterns
Adaptive offloading strategies for dynamic RALM workloads
273× speedup over CPUs, 55× over GPUs, 2.41× over prior accelerators
